 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this claim petition against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Smt. Vinutha.S W/o Rajashekar.J.N, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 24-01-2023 at about 09.00 to 9-05 a.m. while the deceased Smt.Vnutha .S. was riding a Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-02/JK-4948 in order to going her daily work on Tumkur road, when she reached near RMC yard Shell Petrol bunk, at that time,
Private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/D-0072 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, with a high speed and dashed against the deceased two-wheeler from behind and caused the accident.
Due to impact, the said Smt.Vinutha sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter dead body was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah hospital for conducting post morterm.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1.10,000/- towards transportation of deadbody, funeral and final rituals of the deceased.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale, healthy and was aged about 32 years and was working as Accountant in Orion Sutures India Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore and earning Rs.28,000/- p.m and was contributing entire income to welfare of the family.
Due to sudden and tragic death of decesed, the petiitoners are put to great hardship and mental agony and they lost sole earning member of the family.

The (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.977/2023 accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said bus by its driver and in this regard the Yeshwanthpura Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of said bus.

The respondent No.1 being the Insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC Owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a with costs.

sentences.text: On service of notice, the respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective Counsels and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and denied the alleged rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Bus causing accident, death of deceased and also denied age, occupation, income of deceased and dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and admits that this respondent has issued insurance policy in respect of the Private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/D-0072 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contended that driver of the offending vehicle does not posses valid D.L. to drive the same as (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.977/2023 on date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditons of the insurance policy.
It is contended that, the deceased was not wearing the helmet at the time of accident, hence, accident took place due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.

05. The respondent No.2 in her written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and denied the alleged rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Bus causing accident, death of deceased and also denied age, occupation, income of deceased and dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners.

It is admitted that she is the RC owner of the Private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/D-0072 and she got insured the said vehicle with respondent No.1 and hence the respondent no.1 has to indemnify the respondent no.2.
It is contended that, the accident took place due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.

(SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.977/2023 06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Smt.
Vinutha .S. W/o Rajashekar .J.N?
02.

Whether petitioners prove that deceased Smt. Vinutha .S. W/o Rajashekar .J. N died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 24-01-2023 at about 09.00 a.m, on Opposite to Shell petrol bunk, near RMC yard,
Tumkuru road, Bengaluru due to negligent act of driving of the Private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/D-0072 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though he has been elaborately cross- examined by the respondent counsel, but nothing has (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.977/2023 been brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
During the cross-examination by Respondent no.1 counsel he admitted that, at the time of accident the deceased was riding the motor cycle and accident occurred on Tumakuru - Bengaluru main road.

Said road is busy road and denied the suggestion that in the said road no vehicle can go in speed manner and deceased was riding the motor cycle in very high speed and stated that, the offending bus hit against the motor cycle from behind.

The deceased has sustained injuries over her head and denied the suggestion that, accident does not occurred due to negligence of bus driver and denied the suggestion that this accident occurred due to negligence of deceased only.

During the cross examination of Respondent No.2 counsel he admitted that he has not seen the accident and accident road is double road and there is traffic in the morning at 9-00 a.m. and denied the suggestion that, accident occurred due to negligence of his wife.
Also denied the suggestion that, his wife was riding the motor cycle in high speed and skid and fell down and sustained head injury and died.

Further denied to the suggestion that, accident was occurred (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.977/2023 due to negligence on the part of the deceased and not due to driver of the private bus.
12.

On going through the entire oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners, it clearly establishes that deceased Smt. Vinutha .S. w/o Rajashekar .J.N. died in the R.T.A. arising out of accident alleged to have been took place on 24-01-2023 at about 9-00 a.m. near RMC Yard Shell Petrol bunk, on Tumakuru - Bengaluru road due to rash and negligent act of driver of Private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01/D-0072.

It is also proved that the (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.977/2023 petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 is the minor child of the deceased Smt.Vinutha .S. but in the instant case, the petitoiner no.1 is not produced any document to prove that he is also dependant on the earnings of the deceased.

14. The husband can be considered dependant on his wife's income, if he is not currently earning enough to support himself and relies significantly on her income to cover his living expenses,
alhough this would need to be assessed on a case by case basis based on factors like his ability to work, effort to find employment, and defendant the overall financial situation of the couple, in such situations, proving this dependency, might require providing evidence like income records and documentation of unemployment or disability.
15.
The court will assess the husband's ability to earn and where he is genuinely dependent on his wife for financial support.
The husband must show that his financial dependence is not voluntary and that his inability to support himself is due to external factor like illness, disability, job loss etc.,.
In the case on hand the petitioner No.1 is failed to prove that he is also depending upon the earnings of the deceased.

In (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.977/2023 this regard during the cross examination by respondent No.1 counsel he stated that, he is working at Metro Cast Cable Company and getting Rs.15,000/- to 18,000/- p.m. as salary and he getting salary by way of cash.
Therefore, since, he is also one of the earning member of the family, he is not depending upon the earnings of the deceased.

Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative and Issue No.2 is answered Rajashekar J.N vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31157660/

16. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Smt.Vinutha .S. who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
17.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated in the evidence that prior to accident deceased was aged about 32 years and was working as Accountant in Orion Sutures India Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore and earning Rs.28,000/- p.m and was contributing entire income to welfare of the family and they have spent Rs.80,000/- towards funeral and final rituals of deadbody and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation of deadbody.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, they have lost their family member and they put to hardship and agony.
It is duty of the petitioners to prove the age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of the accident.

The petitoners have produced Ex.P13 notarized copy of the aadhaar card of the deceased, Ex.P14 notarized copy of the D.L. of the deceased and Ex.P18 notarized copy of the S.S.L.C. Marks card of the deceased.
Wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 15-08-1990 and the alleged accident occurred on 24-01-2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 33 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 33 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 is 16.
19.

sentences.text: The petitioners have claimed that the deceased was working as Accountant in Orion Sutures India Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore and earning Rs.28,000/- p.m.

To prove the avocation and income of the deceased, they have examined the Accounts Executive in Orion Sutures India Pvt. Ltd., and has produced appointment letter, pay slips, full and final settlement (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.977/2023 letter as Ex.P20 to 22.

During the cross examination made by respondent No.1 counsel he admitted that Ex.P21 pertains to 6 months only and further during the cross examination of respondent counsel he stated that deceased Vinutha was joined to their company as Accounts Executive on 19-04-2022 and denied to the suggestion that, the deceased was not joined their company and not working in their company and unable to say how much amount has paid to family of the deceased with respect to group insurance and he also unable to say how much amount paid towards health benefits of ESI was paid to the legal heirs of the deceased.

Therefore, on gong through oral evidence of PW.2 it appears that, the deceased was working as Account Executive in Orion Sutures India Pvt.
Ltd., Bangalore and as per Ex.P15 appointment letter.
Ex.P16 pay slip for the month of July 2022 to December -2022.
Ex.P20 Appoinment letter , Ex.P21 pay slip from April -2022 to December 2022 and Jan-2023 , Ex.P22 full and final settlement letter.

Which disclose that the deceased was earning monthly salary of Rs.21,000/- p.m. Therefore, this tribunal has taken into consideration of evidence of PW.2 and (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.977/2023 documents produced by him, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at Rs.21,000/- p.m.

sentences.text: In the instant case the no doubt the petitoiner no.1 is the husband of the deceased and petitoner no.2 is the minor daughter of the deceased.
There is no evidence on record to show that the petitioner no.1 is also depending upon the earning of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospectus or additional income of 40% should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged 33 years at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income of the deceased towards future prospectus which would be result in the income to be (21,000 + 8,400) = Rs.29,400/-.
Since the petitioner no.1 is not depend on the earning of the deceased and petitioner no.2 is only dependent

,
as per law, 50% of the income should be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then her monthly income would be (Rs.29,400 - 14,700) = Rs.14,700/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.977/2023 dependency would thus be Rs.14,700/-.
As the deceased was aged about 33 years, the multiplier of 16 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.28,22,400/- (Rs.14,700/- x 12 x 16) towards loss of dependency.

21. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

Accordingly,
in the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.

22. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram and others, reported in AIR online 2018 SC 1249 wherein it is held that the children have entitled for parental consortium of Rs.40,000/- and spousal consortium at Rs.40,000/-.

sentences.text: 23. The claimant No.1 being husband is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and the petitioner No.2 being daughter of the deceased is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.977/2023 consortium and they are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner no.1 is not depending and 50% of the income is taken into consideration towards personal and living expenses of the deceased this tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
Sl. No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency 28,22,400-00 (After deducting 50% of the income towards personal and living expenses)
2. Loss of spousal consortium 40,000-00 (petitioner No.1)
3. Loss of parental 40,000-00 consortium Rajashekar J.N vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31157660/
7 4.
Loss of estate 19,500-00 5.
Funeral expenses and 19,500-00 transportation of dead body Total 29,41,400-00 (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.977/2023 24.

Accordingly, I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.29,41,400/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
25.
Regarding liability:-

In this case, on service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement and denied the entire case of the petitioner and have taken several defences, but they have not lead their evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners.

On perusal of the entire evidence on record, the respondent no.1 admits issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending private bus and respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending private bus.

Hence, respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the owner/insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 being the insurer shall liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.29,41,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within two months (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.977/2023 from the date of this Judgment.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
26. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,41,400/- (Rupees twenty nine lakh forty one thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being husband and petitioner No.2 being minor daughter of the deceased were apportioned the compensation at the ratio of 20% and 80% in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, Petitioner No.1 is entitled to get released 70% share of compensation amount through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account Rajashekar J.N vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31157660/
8 details and remaining 30% of the amount shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank or schedule bank for a period of three years.
